newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro stocks rally, sterling hits 6-year peak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro stocks rally, sterling hits 6-year peak.

text.p: European stocks bounced back in early trade on Friday, encouraged by a strong rally on Wall Street on the back of upbeat corporate earnings.

In currencies, sterling soared to a six-year high of 2.9770 marks as the British currency recovered from initial disappointment at the small size of the Bank of England's quarter percentage point rise on Thursday.

The dollar climbed slightly against the mark as the impact of remarks by Germany's top central banker supporting the mark waned and traders focused on the likely reaction to German budget details due later on Friday.
Frankfurt regained its form after dipping nearly two percent on Thursday to make hefty gains. Dealers said the market rally was likely to keep on rolling as conditions remained ideal.
"I can't think of any negative factors, we have the best of all possible scenarios for the share market," one Frankfurt share trader said.

"My only slight fear is that people are piling into the stock market without really knowing what they are buying." The strong dollar was helping Frankfurt's bull run as it improved prospects for the exporting sector. Investors' optimism was also encouraged by low interest rates and inflation-free growth.

The blue-chip DAX index touched 4,035.93 points in early trade, a gain of over one percent. Frankfurt closed at a record high earlier this week and dealers said the bourse was on course to reach 4,250 points.
Thursday's drop, triggered by the dollar falling more than a pfennig, ended a streak of seven consecutive record closes.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, climbed nearly 0.5 percent after a dull performance on Thursday, lifted by Wall Street and rally in retailing stocks.
"Wall Street should help us, but the main driving factor at the moment is the squeeze in the retail and food retail sectors," said one senior dealer.

New York stocks clawed back part of the previous day's big losses overnight as investors focused on corporate earnings, which have been mostly upbeat so far in the second -quarter reporting period. The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 44.33 points at 7,886.76.

In London, investors were still breathing a collective sigh of relief at the 25 basis-points interest rate hike but some were nervous that the relatively mild monetary tightening left open the possibility of another rate increase in early August.
Richard Jeffrey, head of research at Charterhouse Tilney, said the market was still being supported by high liquidity levels, but added: "There is still worry about interest rates."

In Paris, stocks made only modest advances in light trade ahead of the long Bastille Day holiday weekend. Eurotunnel was up 8.07 percent at 8.70, after shareholders massively backed the company's plan to restructure its 70 billion francs of debt.

On currency markets, sterling powered ahead to 2.9770 marks, its best showing since April 1991, as some traders anticipated further interest rate rises as early as next month. Against the dollar, the pound hit $1.6956, the highest since January 10.

The dollar firmed slightly against the mark. Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer's comments on Thursday that the dollar's rise had gone far enough gave the mark a boost late in the day but dealers said the impact of his remarks was beginning to wane in early Europe.
German retail sale figures data on Friday provided little support for the mark and budget details later were unlikely to bolster the currency.

"There is little reason to be bullish of the mark's prospects and today's data helps underline the need for a strong dollar to help German growth," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was at 113.90 yen and 1.7568 marks compared with 113.12 and 1.7534 in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 14.3 points at 4,782.1.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 46.80 points at 4,039.18.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 3.24 points to 2,932.33.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $320.60 an ounce, compared to Thursday's close of $319.65. Silver at $4.37, up three cents.
